faq.q: What is bottom fishing on a Marbella fishing charter?
faq.a: Bottom fishing involves dropping baited rigs to the seabed to target fish that feed near the bottom. On a Marbella fishing charter, you’ll fish over sandy, rocky, or wreck-strewn grounds at depths of 10–40 metres. Common catches include gilthead bream, grouper, red snapper, and European sea bass. Your skipper will handle anchor positioning and bait selection.

faq.q: Which boats are best for bottom fishing?
faq.a: Any boat from our fleet can be used for bottom fishing. The Astondoa 40 (€749/2h) and Azimut 39 are popular for shorter trips. For longer days, the Mangusta 80 (€4,719/4h) offers extra space and a jet ski. All boats depart from Puerto Banús and include a licensed skipper who knows the best bottom-fishing spots.

faq.q: What species can I catch bottom fishing in Marbella?
faq.a: Typical catches include gilthead bream, common dentex, grouper, red snapper, European sea bass, and occasional stingrays or dogfish. Spring brings bream inshore, summer sees grouper on rocky reefs, and autumn offers snapper on deeper sandy bottoms. Your skipper will adapt techniques based on season and conditions.

faq.q: Do I need a fishing license for a bottom fishing charter?
faq.a: No, you do not need a personal fishing license. The charter includes a licensed skipper and all permits for recreational fishing. However, you must follow Spanish size and bag limits. The skipper will advise on catch-and-release practices and which fish can be kept for cooking.

faq.q: What equipment is provided for bottom fishing?
faq.a: All rods, reels, rigs, bait, and terminal tackle are provided. We use medium-heavy rods with 20–30lb line, ledger or paternoster rigs, and baits like squid, pilchard, or mackerel. You only need to bring sun protection, a hat, and a camera. The skipper will rig everything for the target species.

faq.q: Can I keep the fish I catch and have it cooked?
faq.a: Yes, many local restaurants in Puerto Banús and Marbella will cook your catch for a small fee. The skipper can recommend spots. However, we encourage responsible catch-and-release for protected species. Check with your skipper about current regulations before keeping fish.

faq.q: What is the best time of year for bottom fishing in Marbella?
faq.a: Spring (March–May) offers excellent bream fishing in shallower waters. Summer (June–August) targets grouper and dentex on rocky reefs. Autumn (September–November) is prime for red snapper and sea bass on deeper sandy bottoms. Winter fishing is slower but can yield large dentex. Morning trips often produce more bites.

faq.q: How do I book a bottom fishing charter in Marbella?
faq.a: You can book directly via WhatsApp. For Tier A boats, prices start at €749 for 2 hours. For Tier B boats like the Mangusta 80, the minimum booking is 4 hours at €4,719. All bookings include skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, insurance, and 21% VAT. Contact us for availability and custom durations.

data.body_html:
Bottom fishing from Marbella is one of the most accessible and rewarding ways to fish the Mediterranean. Dropping a baited rig to the seabed off Puerto Banús can yield gilthead bream, grouper, red snapper, and European sea bass. With a Marbella boat charter, you get a licensed skipper who knows the best grounds, all gear included, and a day on the water that combines fishing with the Costa del Sol coastline. Prices start at €749 for 2 hours on a Tier A boat like the Astondoa 40.

How Bottom Fishing Works on a Marbella Fishing Charter

Bottom fishing, also called ledgering or bait fishing, relies on weight to sink a baited hook to the seabed. The rig sits on the bottom or just above it, targeting fish that feed on crustaceans, molluscs, and smaller fish. Your skipper will anchor over sandy patches near rocky reefs, wrecks, or artificial reefs at depths of 10–40 metres. Bait is typically squid, pilchard, or mackerel strips. The technique is simple: cast, wait for a bite, and strike. It's ideal for beginners and experienced anglers alike.

Target Species for Bottom Fishing off Marbella

The Mediterranean offers a variety of bottom-dwelling species. Here’s what you can expect:

  • Gilthead Bream — Abundant in spring, found over seagrass beds and sandy bottoms. Fight hard for their size.
  • Grouper — Larger specimens lurk around rocky reefs in summer. Requires heavier gear and patience.
  • Red Snapper — Autumn favourite on deeper sandy grounds. Delicate white flesh.
  • European Sea Bass — Year-round, but best in autumn. Often caught near structures.
  • Common Dentex — Powerful predator, caught on rocky bottoms in summer and winter.

Your skipper will adjust bait and rig based on the target species. All catches are subject to Spanish recreational fishing limits.

When to Book a Marbella Fishing Charter for Bottom Fishing

Seasonality matters. Spring (March–May) offers the best bream fishing in shallow waters near Cabopino and Cala del Faro. Summer (June–August) targets grouper and dentex on rocky reefs off Estepona. Autumn (September–November) is prime for red snapper and sea bass on deeper sandy bottoms near Sotogrande. Morning trips (8am–12pm) typically produce more bites. Water temperatures range from 14°C in winter to 26°C in summer, affecting fish activity.

What’s Included in Your Bottom Fishing Charter

Every booking includes:

  • Licensed, English-speaking skipper
  • All fishing rods, reels, rigs, bait, and terminal tackle
  • Fuel for the full trip
  • Water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava
  • Light snacks (chips, olives, nuts)
  • Insurance and safety equipment
  • Spanish IVA (21%)

You only need to bring sun cream, a hat, and a camera. The skipper will clean your catch if you plan to have it cooked at a local restaurant.

Techniques and Tips for Bottom Fishing in Marbella

Your skipper will use ledger rigs (running or fixed) with a 2–6oz weight depending on depth and current. Drop-shotting can be effective for sea bass over rocky ground. Bait presentation matters: fresh squid outlasts pilchard. If bites are slow, ask the skipper to move to a different mark. The waters off Puerto Banús have several artificial reefs and wrecks that hold fish. For a more active session, combine bottom fishing with trolling for surface predators.
